clue.text: Place for crossing water an attraction to game

blocks.note: a draw is something that pulls in crowds
the card game

explanation.surface: A tourist spot by a river where the crossing itself becomes a lure for wild animals or sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is a hinged span over a moat, raised and lowered so people can get across.

clue.text: Leaders of delegation in greatly superior accommodation

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letter of each word is wanted

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Heads of a visiting delegation are put up in very grand lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British informal for rented rooms, typically student lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs are lodgings, rooms rented to live in, so they count as a kind of place to stay.

clue.text: Lacking direction, first class mail originally ranked lower

indicators.note: originally takes the word mail back to its beginning, its first letter

blocks.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
the opening letter of mail
less means lower in rank or importance

explanation.surface: Second-class mail goes astray because it ranks below first class.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aimless has no goal or purpose, so it wanders without a set course.

clue.text: Confusion with lager drinkers, perhaps, holding riotous assembly? Exactly!

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so the drinkers surround the riotous word

blocks.note: lager is a beer, so its drinkers are beer men
riotous means wild and unruly
'to a T' means exactly

explanation.surface: A crowd of lager drinkers at a rowdy gathering are left baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: The beer men wrap around WILD, then T from 'to a T' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is a state of being perplexed and puzzled, the same meaning as confusion.

clue.text: Angry when equipment's dropped in water

indicators.note: something dropped in falls inside, so the equipment ends up within the word for angry

blocks.note: irate means angry
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Someone is furious when their gear falls into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' looks like where the equipment lands, but it is a verb meaning to supply with water.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to supply land with water through channels, so the verb water fits.

clue.text: Mineral agreeable to the taste, one hears

indicators.note: one hears means the word is taken as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: nice means pleasant to taste

explanation.surface: Someone praises a mineral that tastes pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The G is silent, so the rock name sounds exactly like nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock made of minerals, so the clue loosely calls it a mineral.

clue.text: One ingredient not used by head cook

indicators.note: something not used is left out, so the ingredient named is dropped from the word for head

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, here a single item that goes into a dish
a head is a chief or leader

explanation.surface: A head cook leaves one ingredient out of the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the I out of CHIEF leaves CHEF; the word chef itself comes from French chef, meaning head.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional kitchen worker who prepares meals, so the word serves as a plain synonym.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman hailing article in beaten gold

indicators.note: metal that is beaten is hammered out of shape, so the letters of gold change order
in places the article inside the other letters

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
the indefinite article
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman greets a piece of hammered gold work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the lower Spanish nobility, a gentleman by birth.

clue.text: State hand-out extremely likely to be accepted without shame

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word likely, its two end letters

blocks.note: Fla is an abbreviation for Florida, a US state
a grant is money handed out
the first and last letters of likely

explanation.surface: A government benefit payment is very likely to be taken without embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests welfare, but it is Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrantly means openly and brazenly, doing something with no attempt to hide it or feel embarrassed.

clue.text: Warned after explosion by spirited quarry manager?

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters of warned land in a new order

blocks.note: game means plucky, willing to have a go
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold quarry boss was told of a blast before it went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' suggests a stone pit with explosions, but here it means hunted animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamewarden looks after hunted animals and birds on an estate, and quarry is the hunted game.

clue.text: Fancy model endlessly portrayed

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word for model is cut off

blocks.note: an ideal is a perfect model to copy

explanation.surface: A glamorous model is shown in an endless photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy model' reads as a glamorous sitter, but fancy is the definition and model gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim of the mind, the same as an idea someone has.

clue.text: Female's name entered in clear desire for company

indicators.note: to be entered in is to be put inside, so the name goes into the word for clear

blocks.note: her is the female possessive
distinct means clear
standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A woman's name is plainly written down out of a wish for friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Herd instinct is the urge in animals and people to group together and follow the crowd.

clue.text: A marksman sure to take toll

blocks.note: first meaning: William ..., the Swiss archer famed for shooting an apple off his son's head
second meaning: to have a marked effect, as when strain begins to show

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sniper certain to kill; the second meaning is the verb in 'the pressure began to tell'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is the legendary sure-shot archer, and the verb means to have a telling, damaging effect.

clue.text: Allure apparent in animated kind of preacher

indicators.note: something apparent in another thing shows up inside it, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person
a spell is a charm or fascination

explanation.surface: A lively preacher's charisma is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospeller is an evangelist who reads or preaches the Gospel, a particular sort of preacher.

clue.text: Inconvenience from dance centre attracting many over the way

indicators.note: attracting draws the next words to stick onto the dance venue, joining them in sequence
in a down answer, over means placed above, so many comes before the way

blocks.note: a disco is a dance venue
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number
a mode is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A nightclub draws crowds across the road, annoying the neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance centre' reads as the middle of a dance, but it is a whole place for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To discommode is to trouble or put someone out, the verb sense of inconvenience.

clue.text: For example, flies around quietly and reconnoitres

indicators.note: the word for the flies goes around the other letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: flies are an example of insects
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Flies buzz around silently while someone scouts the area.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconnoitre is to survey or examine an area closely, which is what someone who inspects does.

clue.text: Neighbour involves little woman in a racket

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the racket wraps around the little woman

blocks.note: taken as written
a din is a loud noise
Jo March, one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: The woman next door gets a small lady mixed up in some scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' hints at a swindle, but here it is noise. The clue is read with A placed before the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbour as a verb means to lie next to, which is exactly what adjoin means.

clue.text: New ammunition about to be turned over to satisfy soldier

indicators.note: turning over flips the order, so those letters read from the other end

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for new
short for ammunition
c is circa, about
to do is to suffice, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A soldier is happy when fresh ammunition is handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a member of an elite raiding unit, a particular kind of fighting man.

clue.text: Row when smoker is confined in study

indicators.note: being confined in something means being held inside it

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
lum is a Scottish word for a chimney, something that smokes

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out when a smoker is shut in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel; it is a line of things. 'Smoker' is not a person but a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A column is a line of figures or people one behind another, a row read in a vertical direction.

clue.text: Spend freely to have a wild bash

blocks.note: first meaning: to splurge money
second meaning: to strike out violently

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild bash' suggests a party where money is spent, but bash here is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to spend money extravagantly and to aim sudden violent blows at someone.

clue.text: Cereal crop entirely covering western county

indicators.note: covering places the crop on top of what follows, so it comes first in the line

blocks.note: corn is a cereal crop
standard abbreviation for west
all means wholly

explanation.surface: Fields of grain blanket a whole county in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the far south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is one of the administrative shires of England, making it a straightforward example of the definition.

clue.text: One accepting credit note to add to collection

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for one holds credit inside it

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards
standard abbreviation for credit
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone takes a credit note to add to their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: An ace is the one in a pack of cards, and te (also spelt ti) is the seventh note of do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by gradual accumulation, gathering more material onto what is there.

clue.text: Source material usable for study programme

indicators.note: raw material is usable for building something new, so these letters are reworked into another word

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Primary documents that a student can use for research.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a planned series of lessons or lectures in a subject, so a syllabus of study.

clue.text: Put on wrong track — error ascribed to motorway design

indicators.note: ascribed to attaches one thing to another, so these words are joined in sequence

blocks.note: M1, the London to Leeds motorway, written as MI
a sin is a wrongdoing
form means shape or design

explanation.surface: A road-planning blunder sends drivers the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; setters often use its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinform is to give someone false information, figuratively sending them down the wrong path.

clue.text: Instant credit

blocks.note: first meaning: a moment
second meaning: buying on ... means buying on credit

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a single phrase, as in instant loans, but each defines the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick is British slang both for a very brief moment and for deferred payment owed to a shop.

clue.text: Quickly run and hide

blocks.note: first meaning: to rush along at speed
second meaning: an animal's skin with the fur on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Run and hide' reads as fleeing, but hide is a noun for an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To pelt is to move fast, and a pelt is the skin of a fur-bearing animal.

clue.text: Piece tossed off back of lorry, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the start of each word, so only their opening letters count

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Something fell off the back of a lorry, the classic excuse for dodgy goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the back of a lorry' is British slang for stolen goods sold cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: An obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, and a coin is a piece that gets tossed.

clue.text: Caught in embrace of remarkably endearing relative

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the word endearing is rendered in an unusual way, its letters reshuffled
being held in an embrace means being surrounded on both sides

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A sweet relative is caught up in a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandniece is the granddaughter of one's brother or sister, a family member.

clue.text: Warms up Cockney food

indicators.note: the London Cockney accent famously drops the aitch at the start of words

blocks.note: heats means warms up

explanation.surface: A Londoner reheats some grub.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London dialect, which drops initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is an informal plural noun for things to eat, a casual term for a meal.

clue.text: Carriage reportedly intended to augment transport

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word for intended is taken by its pronunciation

blocks.note: to deport is to transport someone out of a country
meant means intended

explanation.surface: A railway carriage is said to have been added to boost a transport service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' points to vehicles and transport, but it means the way a person holds themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage and deportment both mean posture, how someone stands, walks and bears their body.
